items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Joe Glaser has been calling me and wants me to come over there with Louie... So that's how I took the job

ctx.x: Well I guess we've come to the point where you went with Louie Armstrong. Spring of 1949.... Let's talk about that.

Okay. Well, see, when Joe Glaser first got that group together, the All Stars, see they called me first before Sid Catlett but I was busy then with my own little group and doing record dates and things around and I just didn't want that gig then to go out on the road. Then I didn't know how the quintet was going to go. And so they got Sid Catlett and the next thing I heard, oh goodness, after the group was about one week old, well

they were a sensation. Sid Catlett, Jack Teagarden, Earl Hines, Barney Bigard, and Louie, they were sensational. And Sid, the group, Velma Middleton singing, and that group just worked and worked and worked until Sid was-took ill, sick, then they couldn't go on the road any more. Sid and I were real tight and when they called me again for the gig I wasn't sure whether Sid was sick or not, but I had Sid's number, I called Sid at his home, they were in New York. I said "Joe Glaser has been calling me and wants me…
